sources_without_edges: NVIDIA v. E. Ohman J:or Fonder AB
Laboratory Corp. of America Holdings v. Davis
scope: Same SCDB argued decision types {1,6} as 2004; whole majority/per-curiam opinions only; Hewitt held for mixed majority/plurality sections. Directed binary links to SCOTUS cases, including majority footnotes.
input_method: Official preliminary-print PDFs; pypdf page-order text plus pdfplumber body flow to bridge page breaks interrupted by footnotes. US Reports and nominative citations resolved via SCDB, official term indexes, and Harvard reporter metadata.
limitations: Citation parsing and PDF segmentation require audits; unresolved or ambiguous references are logged, not guessed.
Different extraction method from 2004 Harvard opinion_index links; comparisons require source-method sensitivity checks.
Binary edges do not measure agreement, importance, or number of mentions.
Only complete US Reports/nominative citations are recognized; short forms alone cannot establish new target identities.
Cited-only nodes have no outgoing citations collected.
DIG per-curiam decisions are included under the same SCDB type/argument rule, and can have zero edges.
Procedural history references are not globally removed; unresolved order citations must be distinguished from missing substantive precedents.
id_policy: Existing 2004 IDs preserved on exact US citation matches; new nodes use us:volume:first_page. Treat IDs as opaque strings.
